fields.sample_size: village case study (Hardiya, southern Bihar; original, dam-resettled and fluoride-resettled households grouped into clusters; household sample about 20% of households per cluster) with interviews, observation and mapping; total n not extracted
fields.effect_estimate: Twenty years of state, non-state and transnational drinking-water interventions have brought technologies and institutions together, but schemes function inadequately (low or no pressure and leakages in resettled areas), producing uneven outcomes across caste and settlement groups; access to clean water remains an open question and infrastructure rearranges social space at village, settlement, cluster and household levels. Qualitative; no effect estimates.
fields.study_design: qualitative single-village case study (ethnographic; interviews and observation)
fields.section: Full text: Methods (village clusters, sample about 20% of households per cluster); findings sections 4-5 (infrastructure and social space); Conclusion
fields.exact_location: Methods (village clusters, sample about 20% of households per cluster); findings sections 4-5 (infrastructure and social space); Conclusion

evidence_level: Single-study evidence: an ethnographic case study of drinking-water infrastructure in one fluoride-affected village of southern Bihar, read in full text 2026-10-04. Inadequate functioning and uneven outcomes across caste and settlement groups after twenty years of interventions.
